Compactness diagnostic for a peak catalog

Source: R/peak_catalog.R
catalog_compactness.Rd

Reports statistics that reveal whether the clustering radius is set correctly. The key statistic is median_obs_per_sample — the typical number of pool peaks each compound catches per sample. A well-clustered catalog has this near 1.0 (each real compound contributes one peak per sample on average). Values noticeably above 1.0 mean the clusters are wide enough to catch multiple distinct peaks from the same sample, indicating over-merging — a looser eps than the true compound-position separation.

Usage

catalog_compactness(catalog, H = 1400L, W = 40L, over_merge_threshold = 1.5)

Arguments

catalog

A peak_catalog object.

H, W

Image dimensions in pixels used to convert location spread from fraction back to pixels. Defaults 1400 x 40 (native GC-DMS). Pass your actual padded / trimmed dimensions for accurate diagnostics.

over_merge_threshold

Cutoff above which a compound is flagged as over-merged. Default 1.5 (a compound catching more than 1.5 pool peaks per sample on average is suspect).

Value

A one-row tibble with compactness statistics. Also invisibly returns the underlying per-compound data if you want to inspect individual compounds via attr(x, "per_compound").

Details

Also reports the distribution of location-spread within compounds (in pixel units at a specified target image size, default native 1400 x 40), and the fraction of compounds passing progressively stricter prevalence thresholds.
